title: rollout-fingerprint-comparator-and-regression-hypothesis-runner
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build the 'Rollout Fingerprint Comparator' — a Console workspace that computes and visualizes compact telemetry fingerprints for route variants and cohorts, lets PMs/engineers run regression hypotheses against those fingerprints, and ties proposed rollouts to an auto-rollback confidence score. The tool complements existing cohort diffs by focusing on multidimensional signatures (latency distributions, token-emission entropy, semantic divergence, error taxonomy) rather than single-metric deltas. It also provides a lightweight 'hypothesis runner' to simulate whether observed differences are likely a signal of regression or expected variance given traffic slices and model randomness.

Motivation: Customers run frequent canaries, A/B tests, and shadow traffic. Current Console delta views surface metric-level changes but still require manual correlation across traces and replays. Engineers waste time assembling the same set of diagnostics to decide on a rollback. This feature reduces time-to-action and increases confidence in automatic fallback policies by producing a small set of interpretable fingerprints and a regression-likelihood estimate.

User stories:
- As an SRE, I want a one-page comparison between baseline and variant that shows compact fingerprints and clickable traces so I can rapidly decide if a canary is safe to promote.
- As a PM, I want to run a hypothesis (e.g., 'increased hallucination for finance prompts') across the affected cohort slices and get a probability and supporting examples.
- As an operator, I want the comparator to surface an auto-rollback confidence score tied to configured SLOs and show the minimal set of failing signals that triggered the score.

Scope (MVP):
- Compute per-variant telemetry fingerprints over a rolling window (24h/1h): latency quantiles, token-rate distribution, top error buckets, semantic divergence score (embedding cosine distance between baseline and variant responses on a sampled prompt set), and response entropy.
- UI: side-by-side fingerprint panel, ranked signal list, per-route sparkline heatmaps, and a trace-link column that opens the trace in the Trace view anchored to the sample.
- Hypothesis runner: accept a predicate (prebuilt: latency, hallucination, response-length) and run bootstrapped resampling to produce a regression-likelihood score and 3 representative examples.
- Auto-rollback advisor: combine regression-likelihood with SLO breach intensity to produce a recommended action and confidence level. Advisor should be advisory in MVP (no automatic action).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Fingerprint computation runs for any route with >1000 requests in window and returns within 20s for a 1h window query.
2) Comparator UI displays side-by-side fingerprints and allows drill-to-trace on at least 3 representative samples per signal.
3) Hypothesis runner returns a deterministic-looking regression-likelihood score (with seedable randomness) and 3 canonical examples within 30s for 1k-sample hypothesis.
4) Advisor computes rollback recommendation with clear rationale (list of contributing signals) and surfaces it in the rollout detail page.
5) End-to-end tests and a demo can show the feature on dedicated CI dataset and the staging Console.

Telemetry & data model notes:
- Storage: use the existing rollout telemetry index but add a compact fingerprint doc per (route,variant,window) keyed by rollout_id, variant_id, window_start. Fingerprint must be small (~2-8 KB).
- Sample selection: deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by rollout_id+variant_id so UI examples are stable across reloads.
- Semantic divergence: compute on embeddings (semantic-driver) using 512-d model; store top-3 high-divergence prompt IDs and mean cosine distance.
- Error taxonomy: normalize error types (timeout, tokenization-fail, model-crash, API-error) and include example responses for non-sensitive cases.

Implementation plan (high level):
- ENG: telemetry ingest pipeline update to compute fingerprints during aggregation. (ENG-3412)
- ENG: service that runs hypothesis jobs on-demand with bootstrap resampling; implement deterministic RNG with explicit seed. (ENG-3799)
- Frontend: Comparator workspace under Console -> Deployment -> Variant view. Wireframes in Figma (link below).
- QA: create synthetic rollout datasets for canary/A-B/shadow scenarios and automated playbooks for acceptance tests.

Wireframes & artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/rollout-fingerprint-comparator (prototype frames annotated)
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODUCT/pages/123456789/Rollout+Fingerprint+Comparator
- Demo notebook: gs://redwood-demos/rollout-fingerprint-demo.ipynb

Release & rollout plan:
- Beta: enable feature behind flag for Dedicated customers and internal orgs. Collect feedback for 2 weeks.
- GA: enable read-only comparator for all Console customers and opt-in advisor for P1 customers tied to SLA.
- Post-GA: iterate on auto-rollback to allow configurable thresholds and throttled automated actions.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: including response examples in UI has PII risk for some customers; need opt-out and masking.
- Cost: additional aggregation compute for fingerprinting may increase billing for heavy customers; explore sampling thresholds.
- False positives: advisor must avoid unnecessary rollbacks. Tune bootstrapping parameters and require signal consensus across >1 signal type.

Next steps:
- Align on fingerprint schema with infra (deadline 2026-02-16).
- Kickoff ENG tickets and wire up telemetry pipeline proofs (ENGs assigned above).
- Frontend spike to validate UI performance on large deployments (ETA 2 weeks).
